D1:
Priority Core is the lowest AnimationPriority (Core < Idle < Movement < Action < Action2-4). The default Animate script plays idle at Idle priority and walk/run at Movement priority, so on every joint those tracks share they outrank your Core swing, and the arms keep following idle/walk. Fix: re-export the animation with priority Action, or set it in code. Also load the track once through the Animator. Humanoid:LoadAnimation is deprecated, and loading on every click piles up tracks.

local char = player.Character or player.CharacterAdded:Wait()
local animator = char:WaitForChild('Humanoid'):WaitForChild('Animator')
local track = animator:LoadAnimation(script.SwingAnim)
track.Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action
tool.Activated:Connect(function()
    track:Play()
end)

Reload the track on CharacterAdded after a respawn.
D2:
1) The camera is client-only. On the server, workspace.CurrentCamera is the server's own unused camera, and changes to it never replicate to players, so nothing happened. 2) On the client, CameraType is still Custom, so the default PlayerModule camera scripts rewrite Camera.CFrame every frame and snap it back behind the character. Fix (LocalScript): 

local cam = workspace.CurrentCamera
cam.CameraType = Enum.CameraType.Scriptable
cam.CFrame = workspace.CutsceneCam.CFrame -- or TweenService between shots
-- when the cutscene ends:
cam.CameraType = Enum.CameraType.Custom
cam.CameraSubject = player.Character:FindFirstChildOfClass('Humanoid')

Wait until CurrentCamera and the cutscene part exist (WaitForChild, because of streaming) before setting them.
D3: CanvasSize is a fixed {0,0},{0,600}. The scrollable area is always 600 px tall whatever the content, so items past 600 px cannot be reached (and with 8 items there is empty space to scroll into). Cleanest fix: set ScrollingFrame.AutomaticCanvasSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y and CanvasSize = UDim2.new(0,0,0,0). The canvas then grows with the UIListLayout content, including padding. Alternative: listen to layout:GetPropertyChangedSignal('AbsoluteContentSize') and set CanvasSize = UDim2.fromOffset(0, layout.AbsoluteContentSize.Y + padding). Also set ScrollingDirection = Y, and size items in offset or with a UIAspectRatioConstraint so the layout height is stable.
D4: Problems: (1) The force is far too small. The part is 20*2*20 = 800 studs^3 at density about 0.7, so it weighs about 560 mass units * 196.2 gravity, roughly 110,000. 5000 cannot lift it. (2) The attachment is at a corner, so the force pushes off-center and creates torque that tips the platform. (3) RelativeTo defaults to Attachment0, so the force is in the part's local space. Once the platform tilts, the 'up' force tilts with it and gains a sideways component, so it slides and spins away. Fix: put the attachment at the part's center (or set ApplyAtCenterOfMass = true), set RelativeTo = Enum.ActuatorRelativeTo.World, and use Force = Vector3.new(0, part.AssemblyMass * workspace.Gravity * k, 0), where k is slightly above 1 to rise and exactly 1 to hover. Recompute if the mass changes. Add an AlignOrientation (or AngularVelocity/torque damping) to keep it level, or a height controller (PID, or AlignPosition / LinearVelocity on Y) for a stable hover height. Give the server or the driver network ownership.
D5:
Leaks: (1) sessions[player] is never cleared, so every player who leaves stays referenced along with their tables. history also grows without limit. (2) Each CharacterAdded makes a new Heartbeat connection that is never disconnected. Every respawn adds another permanent per-frame callback that keeps the old character alive (updateAura on dead characters) and costs CPU. Fixes:

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    sessions[player] = { kills = 0, history = {} }
    player.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(char)
        local conn = RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function() updateAura(char) end)
        char.Destroying:Once(function() conn:Disconnect() end)
        char:WaitForChild('Humanoid').Died:Once(function() conn:Disconnect() end)
    end)
end)
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p) sessions[p] = nil end)

Better: one global Heartbeat loop that iterates the active characters. Cap history (ring buffer) and enable Workspace.PlayerCharacterDestroyBehavior/PlayerDestroyBehavior so old characters and players get destroyed and their connections dropped.
D6:
local function attachPet(pet: BasePart, player: Player)
    local hrp = player.Character:WaitForChild('HumanoidRootPart')
    pet.Anchored = false
    pet.CanCollide = false
    pet.Massless = true
    local a0 = Instance.new('Attachment'); a0.Parent = pet
    local a1 = Instance.new('Attachment')
    a1.Position = Vector3.new(0, 2, 3) -- +Z is behind (LookVector is -Z)
    a1.Parent = hrp
    local ap = Instance.new('AlignPosition')
    ap.Attachment0, ap.Attachment1 = a0, a1
    ap.Responsiveness = 15; ap.MaxForce = 1e6
    ap.Parent = pet
    local ao = Instance.new('AlignOrientation')
    ao.Attachment0, ao.Attachment1 = a0, a1
    ao.Responsiveness = 15; ao.MaxTorque = 1e6
    ao.Parent = pet
    pet.Parent = workspace
    pet:SetNetworkOwner(player) -- smooth on the owner's screen
end

Rules: the pet must be unanchored and must not be welded to the character. Make it CanCollide=false and Massless so it does not push the player. Use AlignPosition plus AlignOrientation in two-attachment mode with the target attachment offset on the HRP, so no per-frame loop is needed (or OneAttachment mode and set .Position/.CFrame on Heartbeat). Responsiveness controls smoothness. Give network ownership to the player, or keep it on the server for authority. Clean up on CharacterRemoving.
D7:
local PFS = game:GetService('PathfindingService')
local path = PFS:CreatePath({
    AgentRadius = 2, AgentHeight = 5, AgentCanJump = true,
    Costs = { Lava = math.huge, Water = 20 },
})
local function walkTo(humanoid: Humanoid, target: Vector3)
    local root = humanoid.RootPart
    local ok = pcall(function() path:ComputeAsync(root.Position, target) end)
    if not ok or path.Status ~= Enum.PathStatus.Success then return false end
    for _, wp in path:GetWaypoints() do
        if wp.Action == Enum.PathWaypointAction.Jump then humanoid.Jump = true end
        humanoid:MoveTo(wp.Position)
        if not humanoid.MoveToFinished:Wait() then return false end
    end
    return true
end

Rules: a Costs entry of math.huge makes a PathfindingModifier label (Lava) untraversable. Material names (Water) take a finite high cost, so they are avoided but still allowed when no dry route exists. Mark the lava with PathfindingModifier.Label = 'Lava'. Wrap ComputeAsync in pcall and check Status. Set humanoid.Jump on Jump waypoints. Listen to path.Blocked and recompute. Call root:SetNetworkOwner(nil) so the server drives the NPC. MoveTo times out after 8 s, so re-issue it per waypoint.

local DSS = game:GetService('DataStoreService')
local Players = game:GetService('Players')
local winsStore = DSS:GetOrderedDataStore('Wins')
local nameCache = {}
local function refresh()
    local ok, pages = pcall(winsStore.GetSortedAsync, winsStore, false, 10)
    if not ok then return end
    for rank, entry in pages:GetCurrentPage() do
        local id = tonumber(entry.key)
        local name = nameCache[id]
        if not name then
            local ok2, n = pcall(Players.GetNameFromUserIdAsync, Players, id)
            name = ok2 and n or ('User '..id); nameCache[id] = name
        end
        updateBoardRow(rank, name, entry.value)
    end
end
while true do refresh(); task.wait(60) end

Rules: OrderedDataStore values must be integers. Keys are strings (tostring(userId)). Sort descending (false) and use pageSize 10. Wrap every call in pcall and respect request budgets: refresh every 60+ s, not per player. Write wins with SetAsync/UpdateAsync on save (not every kill). Cache username lookups. Rendering happens on the server via SurfaceGui, or by replicating the data to clients.

-- (a) music, non-spatial (LocalScript or server)
local music = Instance.new('AudioPlayer')
music.Asset = 'rbxassetid://MUSIC_ID'
music.Looping = true
music.Parent = workspace
local out = Instance.new('AudioDeviceOutput'); out.Parent = music
local w1 = Instance.new('Wire'); w1.SourceInstance = music; w1.TargetInstance = out; w1.Parent = music
music:Play()
-- (b) campfire, spatial
local fire = Instance.new('AudioPlayer')
fire.Asset = 'rbxassetid://FIRE_ID'; fire.Looping = true; fire.Parent = campfire
local emitter = Instance.new('AudioEmitter'); emitter.Parent = campfire
emitter:SetDistanceAttenuation({ [0] = 1, [20] = 0.4, [60] = 0 })
local w2 = Instance.new('Wire'); w2.SourceInstance = fire; w2.TargetInstance = emitter; w2.Parent = fire
fire:Play()

Rules: nothing plays unless it is wired. AudioPlayer goes to AudioDeviceOutput for 2D audio, and to an AudioEmitter parented to a part/attachment for 3D audio. An AudioListener (on the camera or character, created by default via SoundService.DefaultListenerLocation) must hear the emitter, with matching AudioInteractionGroup. Distance falloff comes from the emitter's attenuation curve. Use Asset (not SoundId) and Looping, and preload with IsReady. Effects (AudioEqualizer, AudioReverb, AudioFader) are chained with more Wires.

local MPS = game:GetService('MarketplaceService')
local Players = game:GetService('Players')
local SUB_ID = 'EXP-1234567890'
local function refresh(player)
    local ok, status = pcall(MPS.GetUserSubscriptionStatusAsync, MPS, player, SUB_ID)

Rules: the subscription status is the source of truth. Check it on join and on UserSubscriptionStatusChanged, and do not permanently save 'isVIP' in a DataStore. Revoke the perks when IsSubscribed becomes false. Apply the 2x multiplier on the server at the moment coins are awarded. Wrap calls in pcall, and on failure don't grant (or retry). Subscriptions must give ongoing, recurring benefits with no random rewards, and follow the price and description policies.
D11: Cars: when a player sits, set ownership of the whole car assembly to the driver (VehicleSeat:GetPropertyChangedSignal('Occupant') -> seat:SetNetworkOwner(player); set it back to nil or automatic when they leave). The driver's client then simulates the car with no input-to-physics round trip, which removes the lag. The cost: the owner's client is authoritative over the car's physics, so an exploiter can teleport or fling a car they own. Add server sanity checks (max speed and position delta per step, out-of-bounds checks, ownership only while seated, reset or kick on violation), and never trust client-sent positions for game logic. Guards: call SetNetworkOwner(nil) on the root part (the whole assembly) so the server always simulates them. Otherwise automatic ownership hands an NPC near a player to that player's client, which lets exploiters fling or teleport it. Exploiters can still fling server-owned NPCs through their own character's physics (spinning or high-velocity collisions), so use collision groups between players and guards, clamp guard velocity, and detect abnormal player velocity. In 2026 the Server Authority mode (Workspace.AuthorityMode) can move physics fully to the server with client prediction, which removes most ownership exploits.
D12: Standard DataStores are versioned automatically. Each SetAsync/UpdateAsync/IncrementAsync/RemoveAsync creates a version (with VersionId and CreatedTime), and old versions are kept for 30 days (writes close together may be merged into hourly snapshots). Tool design: (1) an admin-only command or Open Cloud script takes a userId and the update timestamp. (2) Call store:GetVersionAtTimeAsync(key, updateTimeMillis) to get the last version before the update, or ListVersionsAsync(key, Enum.SortDirection.Descending, minDate, maxDate, pageSize) followed by GetVersionAsync(key, versionId). (3) Inspect or validate the data, then write it back with UpdateAsync/SetAsync, which creates a new version, so a bad restore can itself be rolled back. (4) Make sure the player is not online, or release or take over the session lock, so a live server does not overwrite the restore. Kick the player or use a MemoryStore/MessagingService signal. The Open Cloud DataStore API offers the same list/get version endpoints for a web tool. Limits: only 30 days of history. Ordered DataStores have no versioning. Versions count toward request budgets and the 4 MB value limit. Only full values come back, so merge by hand if you want to keep legitimate progress made since the update. Log every restore.
D13: Backend (your server, never the browser) holds Open Cloud API keys with minimal scopes, IP restrictions and audit logging. (1) Announcements: the backend calls the Open Cloud Messaging API (POST https://apis.roblox.com/cloud/v2/universes/{universeId}:publishMessage, topic 'Announcements', scope universe-messaging-service:publish). Every server runs MessagingService:SubscribeAsync('Announcements', ...) and shows the text to clients through a RemoteEvent. Keep messages under 1 KB. Delivery is best-effort and arrives within about a second. (2) Item grants: write a durable pending grant {grantId, itemId} to the player's grant queue, a DataStore key 'grants_<userId>' written through the Open Cloud DataStore API (or a MemoryStore hash/queue with long TTL). Do not edit the player's main save directly, because a live server holding the session would overwrite it. Then publish a 'Grant' message with the userId. If the player is online, the server holding them applies the pending grants at once. Otherwise they are applied on next join. Apply grants idempotently: record applied grantIds in the save, use UpdateAsync, and clear the queue only after saving. The admin panel needs its own auth/2FA, input validation, rate limits and an action log.
D14: BindableEvent/BindableFunction arguments are serialized the same way as remotes. Tables are copied, metatables are dropped, functions are not transferred, and mixed or non-string keys can break. The receiver gets a plain data copy of invObject with no metatable, so invObject:AddItem() is nil and errors. Because it is a copy, mutations also never reach the original. Instances (player) do pass by reference. With ModuleScripts: require() runs a module once per VM and returns the same cached table to every script, so put InventoryService (the class plus a player -> inventory map) in a ModuleScript and have other systems require it and call methods directly on the real object. Real cross-system events become a Signal module (a pure Luau signal that passes values by reference) or callbacks, instead of Bindables. Most teams end up with one or a few entry Scripts that require service modules (single-script architecture), which gives explicit dependencies, typed APIs and shared state without serialization.
D15: UnreliableRemoteEvent suits high-frequency, ephemeral, latest-value-wins data where a dropped or out-of-order packet doesn't matter: aim direction, cosmetic footstep VFX, look angles. Constraints: no delivery or ordering guarantee (packets may drop under load). The payload must be small: about 1000 bytes max per call (around 900 usable), and larger calls are dropped. No return values (no unreliable function). Never use it for hits, damage, purchases, inventory or state transitions, which stay on reliable RemoteEvents/Functions. Moving cosmetic traffic off the reliable channel also stops it from queueing ahead of important events. Still reduce the traffic: send at 10-20 Hz or only on meaningful change, quantize angles (buffer/int16), don't echo back to the sender, cull by distance with FireClient to nearby players instead of FireAllClients, and rate-limit and validate per player on the server, because the client controls the send rate.
D16: Problems: (1) Message size limit is 1 KB, so a 3 KB payload fails to publish. (2) Publish limits per server are about 150 + 60 * players messages per minute, and receive and subscription limits apply per topic and per universe (roughly 10 + 20 * servers messages/min per topic across the universe). 500 servers publishing every 5 s is 6,000 messages/min to one topic, which gets throttled. (3) Fan-out: every server receives every message, about 100 per second each, which is wasteful CPU and memory, and each callback must parse JSON. (4) Delivery is best-effort: no guarantees, no ordering, no persistence. A late subscriber gets no history, and dropped messages leave stale or missing servers with no TTL, so you cannot tell that a server died. Better: each server writes a small entry (JobId, player count, region) into a MemoryStore SortedMap/HashMap with a TTL of about 30 s and refreshes it every 10-15 s. Lobby clients read pages on demand and cached. Use MessagingService only for small, rare events such as invites. Fetch player details lazily.
D17: Limits: HttpService allows about 500 requests per minute per server (all outgoing requests combined, with per-host concurrency limits too). Beyond that requests error or get throttled, and the external API may return 429. HttpEnabled must be on and requests only run on the server. Fix: don't send one call per event. Queue analytics events and batch-flush every 10-30 s, cap the queue, wrap in pcall with exponential backoff and retry, and flush on BindToClose. Consider the built-in AnalyticsService (LogCustomEvent etc.), which uses no HTTP budget. API key: never put it as a literal in a script, since anyone with place access (team members, leaked or uncopylocked places) can read it. Store it in the experience's Secrets (Creator Dashboard secrets with allowed domains) and load it with HttpService:GetSecret('openCloudKey'), passing the Secret object (Secret:AddPrefix('Bearer ')) in headers. Give the key minimum scopes and an IP or experience restriction, and rotate it. Where an in-engine API exists (DataStore, MessagingService, MemoryStore), use it instead of Open Cloud from inside the game.
D18: Camera: Heartbeat (PostSimulation) fires after physics and is not tied to the render frame, so the camera is set against an older character position and jitters. Use RunService:BindToRenderStep('Follow', Enum.RenderPriority.Camera.Value + 1, fn), or RenderStepped/PreRender, so it runs every frame right before rendering, after the character and input update. Use the dt argument, and lerp with 1 - math.exp(-k*dt) for frame-rate-independent smoothing. Server projectile: RenderStepped, PreRender and BindToRenderStep exist only on the client because the server does not render. Use Heartbeat/PostSimulation (after physics; good for moving things and checking hits) or Stepped/PreSimulation (before physics), and scale movement by deltaTime. Modern names: PreRender (RenderStepped), PreAnimation, PreSimulation (Stepped), PostSimulation (Heartbeat).
D19: Use the Input Action System (IAS). In 2026 it is the recommended path for new cross-platform games, and ContextActionService is legacy (still works, not deprecated outright). Structure, built as instances (in Studio or code): InputContext (a group of actions with Enabled, Priority and Sink, e.g. 'OnFoot' and 'Vehicle' contexts you switch) -> InputAction (Type such as Bool for interact/sprint, Direction1D/2D/3D, ViewportPosition; events Pressed, Released, StateChanged; GetState()) -> InputBinding children (KeyCode = LeftShift or ButtonL3, a PrimaryModifier/SecondaryModifier for combos, UIButton = a GuiButton for touch, plus composite direction keys like Up/Down/Left/Right). Gameplay code listens to actions instead of devices, so rebinding and new devices only change bindings. Default player scripts: Roblox is moving the default movement and camera controls (the PlayerModule ControlModule/CameraModule) onto IAS-based, engine-provided controls. Forking the old PlayerModule Lua is being phased out in favour of configuring or overriding the default InputContexts and actions, so avoid building on a copied PlayerModule.
D20: Server Authority (2026 beta, then release): enable it on Workspace (AuthorityMode = Server, Workspace.AuthorityMode property / experience setting), which uses fixed-rate physics stepping. What it does: the server owns and simulates all physics, including player characters, so clients lose network-ownership authority. Each client predicts its own character and objects locally with the same input, the server resimulates authoritatively, and clients reconcile and roll back on mismatch. That removes teleport, fly, speed and fling exploits that come from client ownership. Script changes: (1) Movement and ability logic that changes physics must be deterministic and run on both client and server inside RunService:BindToSimulation(fn) at the fixed step, using the provided deltaTime, not RenderStepped/Heartbeat. (2) Read player input through the Input Action System (InputActions replicate to the server for prediction) instead of client-only state or remotes for movement. (3) Remove SetNetworkOwner and client-ownership tricks, and client-side CFrame teleports of the character. (4) Cosmetic effects stay client-side, and hitbox/combat code uses server state (with rewind if needed). Test with network simulation on.
D21: Use RunService:BindToSimulation (2026), which runs your callback at a fixed simulation timestep (for example 60 Hz) on both client and server, independent of render FPS. A 30 FPS and a 144 FPS client then run the same number of identically sized steps, and the server can resimulate the same steps for authoritative prediction and rollback (Server Authority). Requirements: Workspace physics must use fixed stepping (PhysicsSteppingMethod Fixed / Server Authority enabled). The callback must be deterministic: use only the fixed deltaTime it receives, the simulation state, and replicated input from the Input Action System, with no os.clock, RenderStepped data, camera or random values unless seeded. Use the same module on client and server. Keep it cheap because it may run several times per frame, or be re-run during rollback. Don't yield or have side effects (VFX, sounds, remotes) inside it.
D22: Lighting.Technology could never be set from game scripts (it is a Studio/plugin-level property), so the LocalScript errors. Roblox has also deprecated Technology in favour of the unified lighting system. Studio now shows Lighting.LightingStyle (Realistic vs Soft) and Lighting.PrioritizeLightingQuality instead of the Technology dropdown, and the engine picks the best renderer the device can handle (Future-quality where supported, scaled down automatically on weaker hardware). Quality is driven by the player's graphics level, not by a per-experience technology switch. For a settings menu, expose only what is allowed at runtime (shadows/post-effects toggles, ColorCorrection, Atmosphere, or setting lighting properties like GlobalShadows client-side) and remove the Technology assignment.
D23:
Yes. Instance:QueryDescendants (2025) takes a selector string (the same syntax as UI styling selectors: class, .Tag, [$attribute] filters), so the engine does the filtering:

local coins = workspace:QueryDescendants('BasePart.Coin[$Collected = false]')
for _, coin in coins do
    -- ...
end

'BasePart' matches by class (including subclasses), '.Coin' is the CollectionService tag, and '[$Collected = false]' is the attribute filter. Alternative: CollectionService:GetTagged('Coin') filtered by IsA('BasePart') and GetAttribute('Collected') == false. Both beat a full GetDescendants() scan every round.
D24: All four have built-ins: math.lerp(a, b, t) replaces lerp, math.map(x, inMin, inMax, outMin, outMax) replaces remap, math.isnan(x) replaces x ~= x (with math.isinf and math.isfinite alongside), and buffer.readbits(buf, bitOffset, bitCount) / buffer.writebits(buf, bitOffset, bitCount, value) replace manual shifting to pack 3-bit and 5-bit fields. All of these shipped in 2025 Luau.
